profile.reading: This record is named Centrale TIM Trento Nord in this registry, mapped near Trento, Italy. Centrale is Italian for exchange, and this name pattern is consistent with a legacy TIM telephone exchange building rather than one of the modern, Noovle branded data centers in TIM Enterprise own certified network, which the operator own most recent published network overview does not list a Trento facility among. No corporate source describing this specific building as a data center, with any capacity or certification detail, was found this session, so address, capacity, and square footage remain not published in this record. Noovle's current 16-site national network, spanning Turin, Milan, Padova, Bologna, Rome, and Florence, does not include a Trento facility, reinforcing this entry's assessment that Centrale TIM Trento Nord most likely represents legacy TIM telephone-exchange infrastructure rather than a modern Noovle-branded commercial data center. TIM (Telecom Italia) is Italy's former state telephone monopoly, privatized in the 1990s, and like many former national telecom monopolies elsewhere in this registry (compare CenturyLink/Lumen's legacy US central offices), it retains a much larger network of older exchange buildings across the country than the handful now marketed as certified colocation-grade data centers under its modern Noovle brand. This registry does not assert this building's current operational status, capacity, or any technical specification without a source describing it directly, and none was located this session. A further search this session, using web search tools unavailable in the prior exhausted pass, located coverage of TIMs Trentino copper network shutdown, but the only named exchange in that reporting is the TIM central office at Mattarello, a district on the opposite side of Trento from this rows Trento Nord name, serving about 2,000 phone lines with FTTH cabling completed there. No source found this session names a Trento Nord exchange specifically or describes this building as a Noovle branded data center, reinforcing the prior assessment that this is most likely a legacy telephone switching facility outside Noovles published 16 site commercial data center network rather than a colocation grade data center.
